From 2,266 seedlings of a 1921 cross between POJ 2364 and EK 28, Jeswiet selected POJ 2878, which was tested and released in 1925. Within a decade it covered most of Java's cane land, lifted sugar yields and was planted from India to Louisiana and Brazil. Most commercial canes bred since carry it in their pedigrees, which earned it name 'wonder cane of world'.

bbc-founded-1922.summary: In 1922 Britain formed the BBC as a single licensed broadcaster, a model for public service radio and television worldwide. It made its first official broadcast in November, and Scottish Calvinist John Reith became general manager in December. On 1 January 1927 it became the British Broadcasting Corporation, a public body under royal charter funded by licence fees.

urea-stibamine-brahmachari-1922.summary: Physician Upendranath Brahmachari, working at Campbell Medical School in Calcutta with almost no laboratory, prepared urea stibamine, a pentavalent antimony compound, in 1920 and reported clinical trials in 1922. It cured over ninety percent of kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis) cases, a disease then killing tens of thousands a year in Assam and Bengal. Earlier tartar emetic treatments needed many painful injections and often failed. Assam's health department adopted urea stibamine in mass campaigns from 1923 and kala-azar deaths fell steeply. Brahmachari was nominated for Nobel Prize in 1929, and pentavalent antimonials remained standard leishmaniasis drugs for decades.

ypf-founded-1922.summary: In 1922 Argentina created YPF, the first state oil company to run everything from wells to petrol pumps, a model many countries copied. It handled exploration, production, refining and sales. First director Enrique Mosconi sought national control of oil supplies to strengthen Argentina's independence; its La Plata refinery, opened in December 1925, then ranked tenth largest worldwide.

bose-statistics-1924.summary: In 1924 Satyendra Nath Bose sent Einstein a paper counting photons in a new way; Einstein extended it, and bosons bear his name. Einstein translated it into German and arranged publication; it came out in 1924. Bose had derived Planck's radiation law by treating light quanta as identical, indistinguishable particles that could crowd into the same state; Einstein extended the method to atoms. Particles that obey Bose-Einstein statistics are now called bosons.

hubble-andromeda-galaxy-1924.summary: In 1924 Hubble showed Andromeda lay far outside the Milky Way, a galaxy of its own; our universe grew by a factor of billions. Astronomers then mostly held that our Milky Way was the entire universe. Cepheids pulse at rates tied to their true brightness, as Henrietta Swan Leavitt had found in 1908, so they serve as distance markers; Hubble's observations, begun with an October 1923 plate and announced in January 1925, showed Andromeda was far too distant to be part of our galaxy and was an entire galaxy outside it.

technion-opens-1924.summary: In 1924 Technion opened in Haifa after a fight over whether to teach in German or Hebrew. Zionist delegates had first discussed such an institute at their Fifth Congress in Basel in 1901. Choosing Hebrew, in what was called the War of the Languages, helped establish Hebrew as Israel's official language; Technion is now Israel's oldest university and underpins its high-tech industry.

walker-southern-oscillation-1924.summary: As Director General of Observatories in India from 1904, Gilbert Walker set teams of Indian computers in Simla and Pune to calculate correlations between rainfall, pressure and temperature records worldwide in search of monsoon predictors after famines of 1890s. In 1924 he named a see-saw of surface pressure between Indian Ocean and eastern Pacific the Southern Oscillation. Later work by Bjerknes linked it to El Nino, giving ENSO, now central to seasonal forecasting for farmers across tropics. Walker's statistical method, including what became Walker's test for significance of periodogram peaks, grew from a practical need: forecasting rains that decided harvests for hundreds of millions.

It showed a head belonging to a ventriloquist's dummy called Stooky Bill in a 32-line image at five pictures per second. Earlier that year he had shown only moving silhouettes, at Selfridges department store in London; he now fetched office worker William Edward Taynton, 20, who became television's first human subject, and on 26 January 1926 gave his first public demonstration of true television images.

gandhi-charkha-spinners-association-1925.summary: In September 1925 Mohandas Gandhi founds the All-India Spinners' Association (Akhil Bharat Charkha Sangh) to organise hand spinning and production and sale of khadi, hand-spun and hand-woven cloth. Its constitution, printed in Young India on 1 October 1925, declares that an expert organisation to develop hand-spinning and khaddar is now needed, "a permanent organisation, unaffected and uncontrolled by politics". Charkhas, low portable spinning wheels, had appeared on a prototype Congress flag since 1921, and Congress members were asked to spin half an hour a day. Lisa Trivedi's Journal of Asian Studies article shows how 1920s khadi exhibitions turned a household tool into a visual map of a nation. A folding charkha Gandhi sent Henry Ford in 1941 survives in the Henry Ford museum.

gezira-scheme-1925.summary: In 1925 Sennar Dam began irrigating the Gezira plain in Sudan for cotton; a colony's economy was built on one crop and one dam. Egyptian-type long-staple cotton had grown there since 1904, promising raw material for British textile mills, and irrigation began on 24 square kilometres in 1914; after the lowest Nile flood in 200 years, Sennar's 3-kilometre dam was built, financed first by Sudan Plantations Syndicate and then guaranteed by Britain. Cotton remained the region's main crop, and by 2008 irrigation covered 8,800 square kilometres.

heisenberg-matrix-mechanics-1925.summary: In 1925 Heisenberg wrote the first consistent quantum mechanics, atoms as arrays of numbers, which Born and Jordan completed with him in 1926. It represented physical observables as matrices that evolve in time and described quantum jumps without Bohr's sharply defined electron orbits. Erwin Schrödinger's wave mechanics, published months later, proved equivalent to it; Heisenberg received physics' 1932 Nobel Prize.

lilienfeld-fet-patent-1925.summary: In 1925 Lilienfeld patented a solid-state device to control current with an electric field, the transistor's idea 22 years early. It described a solid-state device in which an electric field controls current through semiconductor material, doing vacuum tubes' work. Without high-purity semiconductors he was never able to build a working device, and he published nothing in journals, so his patent won little notice. US Patent 1,745,175 was granted in 1930; when Bell Labs' Brattain and Bardeen sought patents on their 1947 transistors, most of their claims were rejected because of Lilienfeld's.

Town boosters staged his trial to draw publicity, with American Civil Liberties Union lawyers defending; Scopes was unsure he had ever taught evolution but incriminated himself so that there was a defendant. William Jennings Bryan prosecuted against defense lawyer Clarence Darrow; Scopes was fined $100, overturned on a technicality, and radio's first nationally broadcast trial publicized America's fundamentalist-modernist controversy.

By the end of March 1926, its Kariya plant had added 240 Type G looms, and 520 were operating by September's end; Hioki-cho built 1,023 before Toyoda Automatic Loom Works took over.

Civil aviation had grown from Post Office airmail routes begun in 1918, and aviation leaders had pressed for federal safety regulation. It created an Aeronautic Branch in the United States Department of Commerce with powers to test and license pilots, certify aircraft, make and enforce safety rules, establish airways, maintain navigation aids and investigate accidents. William P. MacCracken Jr. was its first head; it became the Bureau of Air Commerce in 1934.

In 1949, legislation renamed it Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO); its later developments include atomic absorption spectroscopy, essential components of early Wi-Fi, and the first commercially successful polymer banknote.

He called its contents "scientifiction" in the style of Jules Verne, H. G. Wells and Edgar Allan Poe; such stories had appeared only occasionally in general magazines, and nobody had yet coined science fiction as a term. Circulation reached 150,000, and Gernsback added readers' discussion pages in 1927 and Amazing Stories Quarterly in 1928, helping define his genre.

Burning gasoline with liquid oxygen, it rose 41 feet and flew 184 feet in 2.5 seconds. Liquid propellants can be throttled and carry far more energy than gunpowder, which had powered rockets for centuries. Ridiculed by press and fellow scientists for his spaceflight theories, Goddard grew secretive; he was recognized after his death as one of the founding fathers of modern rocketry.

He continued with photoelectric cells and vacuum tubes, built an iconoscope camera in 1935 and demonstrated an all-electronic system that November. His group at NHK began test broadcasts in Tokyo in 1939 and ran weekly experimental programmes until war stopped them in June 1941. After 1945 he led television development at Victor Company of Japan.

wallace-hybrid-corn-hi-bred-1926.summary: Editor and plant breeder Henry A. Wallace incorporates Hi-Bred Corn Company in Des Moines on 20 April 1926, the first firm devoted to hybrid seed corn. His Copper Cross hybrid had won the 1924 Iowa Corn Yield Test, and he built on Donald Jones's double-cross method of 1917 to 1918 at Connecticut's experiment station, which made inbred-line hybrids commercially viable. Farmers must buy new seed each year because hybrid vigor collapses in saved seed, so Wallace's business model holds. Iowa hybrid acreage rises from under 1 percent in 1933 to 6 percent in 1935, 50 percent in 1938 and near 100 percent by 1942. Zvi Griliches's 1957 Econometrica study fit logistic curves to this spread and explained timing by profitability, founding diffusion economics.

Uda published a series of Japanese papers from 1926, and Yagi presented a summary in English to Institute of Radio Engineers in 1928, which carried design abroad. Japanese military showed little interest, while British and American radar sets in Second World War used Yagi arrays; rooftop television aerials later made it familiar worldwide.

ge-monitor-top-refrigerator-1927.summary: In 1927 General Electric introduces its Monitor Top, a steel cabinet with its sealed compressor mounted in a round housing on its lid, the first electric refrigerator to become widely popular in American homes, Smithsonian curators say. indian-broadcasting-company-radio-1927.summary: Indian Broadcasting Company, a private firm licensed by Government of India, opened a medium wave station in Bombay on 23 July 1927 and another in Calcutta a month later, after amateur radio clubs had broadcast since 1923. Programmes mixed Hindustani music, English talks and market reports for a few thousand licence holders. The company went bankrupt in 1930; government took over as Indian State Broadcasting Service and renamed it All India Radio in 1936, with Lionel Fielden expanding stations to Delhi, Madras and Lahore. Radio carried Nehru's independence speech in 1947 and remains India's widest reaching public medium through Akashvani.

Its Vitaphone system played sound from discs locked to its projector, carrying six songs by Al Jolson and his ad-libbed line "Wait a minute, wait a minute, you ain't heard nothin' yet". Spoken dialogue filled barely two minutes, in isolated sequences, yet its success made sound films commercially dominant and effectively ended silent cinema.

That service passed through colonial-era Kenya Broadcasting Service to become Kenya Broadcasting Corporation in 1961.

transatlantic-radiotelephone-1927.summary: In January 1927 telephone calls crossed the Atlantic by radio at $75 for three minutes; voices spanned an ocean before any cable could. Submarine cables had carried telegraph traffic since 1858, but voice needed amplifiers along its route, and a telephone cable, discussed from the 1920s, required advances that arrived only two decades later. Radio telephony remained Europe's and North America's only voice link until TAT-1, laid between Oban in Scotland and Clarenville in Newfoundland, opened on September 25, 1956 with 36 channels.

uncertainty-principle-1927.summary: In 1927 Heisenberg showed a particle's position and momentum cannot both be known exactly, a limit on knowledge built into nature. He had realised in March 1926, at Bohr's institute, that his quantum mechanics made such quantities non-commuting, and worked out his idea in letters to Wolfgang Pauli. Earle Kennard that year and Hermann Weyl in 1928 proved that position and momentum spreads multiply to at least half Planck's reduced constant.
